title: The High Provision
premise: Wendell Lockridge, a riverboat captain who measures life in miles rather than years, is hired by her old rival Odile Marchetti to run one last expedition up the Thessaly River before the glacier calving season closes the high route for good. The cargo is sealed, the manifest is false, and the job was sworn off three years ago after an accident that took Wendell's brother and her memory of the final night. As the crew climbs toward the High Provision — a stranded supply cache that may hold proof of what really happened — Wendell's recovered fragments begin to contradict the story Odile has told everyone. At the calving fields, the truth surfaces: the accident was sabotage, and the cache holds the evidence. Wendell must choose between the loyalty she owes her found family aboard and the truth they all deserve, running the river home through the brief open window as the ice comes down behind them.
about_author: Hazel Thackeray spent a decade working seasonal river runs in the northern territories before turning to fiction full-time. She writes adventure novels about people who love hard places too much to leave them.

chapters.title: Miles, Not Years
chapters.summary: Wendell's POV. Three years after her brother Tom's death, Wendell pilots the Coriander on routine freight runs, keeping grief at bay with schedules and sandbars. Her crew — engineer Bo, cook Sefa, deckhand Priya — has become her family by unspoken agreement. The beat: comfortable numbness about to be disturbed.

chapters.title: The Woman at the Dock
chapters.summary: Wendell's POV. Odile Marchetti appears at the dock with a contract: one run upriver, triple pay, sealed cargo, no questions. She and Wendell share a history neither will name. Wendell refuses; then Odile mentions the route opens for six weeks only. The beat: old wounds reopened on a public dock.

chapters.title: Crew Meeting
chapters.summary: Priya's POV. Wendell lays out the offer honestly, omitting only her history with Odile. Money would clear their debts and refit the aging boat. Bo votes yes immediately; Sefa smells trouble; Priya watches Wendell flinch at the word 'upriver.' The beat: found family weighing loyalty against instinct.

chapters.title: Terms of Passage
chapters.summary: Wendell's POV. Wendell signs, setting her own conditions: she chooses the route, no passengers beyond Odile's two 'surveyors,' and anyone can walk away at any stop. Odile agrees too easily. That night Wendell finds her old river journal missing from its lockbox. The beat: dread disguised as professionalism.

chapters.title: Loading the Sealed Crates
chapters.summary: Bo's POV. The surveyors — quiet man Voss, cheerful woman Ansel — supervise loading crates stamped with a mining company logo Bo doesn't recognize. One crate hums faintly when he leans against it. He says nothing, but starts a private tally of oddities. The beat: first crack in the official story.

chapters.title: Departure at First Light
chapters.summary: Sefa's POV. The Coriander leaves port with a small farewell crowd; Sefa notices who isn't there — Tom's old fishing partner, who once swore never to speak to Wendell again. Sefa serves a departure breakfast nobody finishes. The beat: tenderness shadowed by the sense of a door closing.

chapters.title: The Mood of the Water
chapters.summary: Wendell's POV. Early river chapters establish Wendell's genius: reading current, gravel bars, and bird behavior. She takes a shortcut Odile's charts say is impossible, proving her worth and quietly reasserting control. Odile watches with something like respect. The beat: competence as armor.

chapters.title: Ansel's Questions
chapters.summary: Priya's POV. Ansel, friendly and curious, asks Priya about the boat's past and lets slip knowledge of the Coriander's last upriver trip — the one that killed Tom. Priya deflects but reports it to Wendell, who goes very still. The beat: the past knocking politely at the door.

chapters.title: First Rapids
chapters.summary: Wendell's POV. A technical, thrilling run through the Kestrel Narrows. Voss panics and grabs the wheel; Wendell breaks his wrist against the rail without slowing the boat. Afterward, Odile apologizes smoothly and doubles the hazard pay. The beat: Wendell's authority tested and confirmed.

chapters.title: What Bo Found Below
chapters.summary: Bo's POV. Repairing a fouled intake, Bo finds a welded compartment under the hold containing rope, a broken carabiner, and a nameplate: T. LOCKRIDGE. He sits in the dark bilge a long time. The beat: grief discovered secondhand, loyalty complicated.

chapters.title: Sefa's Kitchen Confessions
chapters.summary: Sefa's POV. Sefa cooks dinner and gets each crew member alone in turn, drawing out what they're carrying. We learn Sefa lost a daughter and chose this floating family deliberately. Sefa warns Wendell: secrets rot faster in close quarters. The beat: warmth as reconnaissance.

chapters.title: The Town Called Reprieve
chapters.summary: Multiple POVs. Resupply stop where anyone may leave. Nobody does — even when Odile posts the true destination on the harbor board: the High Provision cache, above the calving fields. Wendell realizes the crew is choosing this. The beat: commitment made visible.

chapters.title: Odile's Version
chapters.summary: Odile's POV (first alternate). On the porch of the harbormaster's office, Odile tells Wendell a polished story: the expedition is salvage, the cache holds equipment she financed, Tom's death was weather, not fault. Wendell almost believes her. Almost. The beat: seduction of a comforting lie.

chapters.title: Fragments
chapters.summary: Wendell's POV. Night terrors bring back sensory shards of the accident: cracking ice, a shout in Odile's voice, cold water, Tom's lantern sinking. Wendell wakes with the word 'provision' in her mouth and doesn't know why. The beat: memory returning as threat rather than gift.

chapters.title: Voss Talks in His Sleep
chapters.summary: Priya's POV. Standing night watch, Priya hears Voss mutter coordinates and the phrase 'before the season turns.' She copies the coordinates. Cross-checking charts, she finds they mark a point upstream of any legal claim. The beat: curiosity hardening into suspicion.

chapters.title: The Portage
chapters.summary: Bo's POV. The crew hauls the Coriander over a two-mile land bypass. Brutal labor becomes bonding; Ansel works hardest and tells Bo about her sister she couldn't save, mirroring Wendell and Tom. Bo begins to suspect Ansel is more hostage than conspirator. The beat: empathy across enemy lines.

chapters.title: High Water Country
chapters.summary: Wendell's POV. The river narrows into glacial meltwater, fast, cold, and unpredictable. Wendell must navigate by sound — listening for the pitch of water over stone. A near-capsize bonds the crew in shared terror and laughter afterward. The beat: fear transmuted into trust.

chapters.title: The Ledger
chapters.summary: Sefa's POV. Cleaning the surveyors' cabin, Sefa finds a ledger listing payments to a name she recognizes: the harbormaster from Reprieve, and someone signed only 'L.' She photographs it and gives it to Wendell, who recognizes her own initial and feels sick. The beat: evidence pointing inward.

chapters.title: Confrontation at the Fireline
chapters.summary: Wendell and Odile, two-hander. Wendell shows Odile the ledger and demands the truth. Odile counters with a partial confession — there was a deal gone wrong, money moved — but insists Tom's death was an accident and that Wendell herself agreed to the plan that night. The beat: the ground tilting under everything Wendell believes.

chapters.title: Did I Agree?
chapters.summary: Wendell's POV. Shaken, Wendell interrogates her own blanks. She digs out the ship's log from the old voyage, kept in the welded compartment Bo found. Pages for the final week are torn out — but the binding impressions remain, readable by raking light. The beat: detective work born of self-doubt.

chapters.title: Impressions
chapters.summary: Priya's POV. Priya, a former archivist, recovers ghost text from the log: entries showing Tom had discovered the cache weeks early and logged its contents — including something marked 'do not move before inspection.' The last legible line is in Tom's hand: 'O. knows. Tell W.' The beat: the dead brother speaking.

chapters.title: Mutiny Weather
chapters.summary: Bo's POV. Bo shares the nameplate with the crew. Anger moves through the boat like weather. Sefa argues for confronting Odile now; Priya argues for waiting until they have the whole picture; Bo wants to turn around. Wendell holds course north. The beat: family fracturing under load.

chapters.title: Ansel Breaks
chapters.summary: Ansel's POV (second alternate). Ansel confesses to Wendell: she and Voss were hired to verify the cache contents and destroy anything incriminating. She came because the company destroyed her sister's village and she wanted leverage. She gives Wendell the real manifest. The beat: defection, and the cost of choosing sides.

chapters.title: The Real Cargo
chapters.summary: Wendell's POV. The manifest reveals the crates hold core samples and documents proving the mining company knowingly poisoned the upper river — and that Odile's original expedition was meant to expose it before someone bought her silence. Tom died protecting the evidence. The beat: the mission inverts.

chapters.title: Ice Ahead
chapters.summary: Wendell's POV. The calving season is starting early — distant booms like artillery. The window home is shrinking from weeks to days. Odile, confronted, admits she sold out but claims she hired Wendell to finish what Tom started, as penance. Wendell doesn't know whether to believe her. The beat: motive revealed, trust still broken.

chapters.title: Vote at the Confluence
chapters.summary: Full crew scene. Wendell lays out everything — the evidence, the danger, the shrinking window — and puts it to a vote: take the cache and run the gauntlet home, or abandon it and live. All six vote to go, including, unexpectedly, Voss. The beat: found family choosing truth together.

chapters.title: The Climb to the Cache
chapters.summary: Bo's POV. Offloading crates onto sledges, the crew hauls up the moraine toward the High Provision. Glacial groans punctuate the climb. Voss proves competent and brave, earning his place. A serac collapse nearly kills Priya; Bo saves her. The beat: peril forging the team's final shape.

chapters.title: Tom's Camp
chapters.summary: Wendell's POV. They find Tom's last camp, preserved in ice: his notes, photographs, and a letter addressed to Wendell he never sent. Reading it, Wendell remembers the final night — she was there, she tried to stop the sabotage, and her memory broke under the guilt of failing. The beat: devastating restoration of memory.

chapters.title: The Letter
chapters.summary: Wendell's POV, intimate. Tom's letter, quoted at length: he forgave her in advance, asked her to keep living in miles, and named the saboteur — not Odile, but the company man who became the harbormaster of Reprieve. Odile's betrayal was smaller and sadder: silence bought with threats. The beat: grief reframed as inheritance.

chapters.title: Calving
chapters.summary: Ensemble action chapter. The glacier calves massively while the crew is on the ice field. They race collapsing terrain to reach the cache vault, digging it free as the route behind them fills with brash ice. Voss is injured shielding the documents. The beat: nature indifferent to human stakes.

chapters.title: The High Provision
chapters.summary: Wendell's POV. Inside the vault: Tom's complete evidence, plus supplies he stockpiled for whoever came next — food, fuel, spare parts, a note reading 'for the crew who finishes this.' Wendell understands the title at last. The beat: revelation and provision as one.

chapters.title: Odile's Choice
chapters.summary: Odile's POV. With the evidence in hand, Odile must decide: destroy it and protect her bargain, or broadcast it and lose everything. Watching Wendell's crew, she chooses exposure, transmitting the archive via the cache's emergency beacon and accepting arrest will follow. The beat: redemption purchased at full price.

chapters.title: Running Home
chapters.summary: Wendell's POV. The descent: a white-knuckle run down a river choking with ice, using every trick Wendell knows, the crew moving as one organism. The Coriander takes damage but holds. Behind them, the route closes for the year. The beat: mastery and grace under maximum pressure.

chapters.title: The Harbormaster's Net
chapters.summary: Tension spike. At Reprieve, the corrupt harbormaster tries to seize the boat and burn the evidence. Standoff on the dock; the townspeople, whose water the poison reached, side with the crew. Voss, half-healed, testifies. The beat: truth finding allies in ordinary people.

chapters.title: Aftermath Ashore
chapters.summary: Sefa's POV. Officials arrive; statements are taken; the company's cover begins to crack publicly. There are hearings ahead, but tonight there is a meal on the dock — Sefa cooking for strangers and crew alike, feeding the town that stood with them. The beat: exhale, gratitude, community.

chapters.title: What Odile Owes
chapters.summary: Wendell and Odile, final two-hander. No forgiveness yet, maybe ever — but an accounting. Odile accepts charges; Wendell gives her Tom's unsent letter to read in custody. 'You don't get absolution,' Wendell says. 'You get the truth. It's heavier.' The beat: justice without cheap mercy.

chapters.title: Refit
chapters.summary: Bo's POV. Weeks later, the crew rebuilds the Coriander properly — new planking, the welded compartment opened to daylight and turned into a memorial shelf for Tom's things. Debts cleared by salvage rights. The beat: repair as ritual, grief given a place to live.

chapters.title: Season's Turn
chapters.summary: Priya's POV. News breaks nationally; the river is slated for protection. Priya archives the expedition records, deciding some truths belong in daylight and some — like Ansel's sister's name — deserve monuments instead of headlines. The beat: memory honored, purpose renewed.

chapters.title: Open Water
chapters.summary: Wendell's POV. Spring. The route opens again, clean and bright. Wendell takes the Coriander upriver with her full crew and Tom's letter framed at the helm. She still measures life in miles — but now the miles are hers, chosen, shared. Final line echoes the opening. The beat: arrival, not escape.

chapters.title: The Crew Who Finishes This
chapters.summary: Ensemble coda, rotating short POVs. One year on: Sefa teaching river kids to cook, Bo apprenticing young engineers, Priya publishing the archive, Ansel rebuilding her sister's valley, Voss serving his reduced sentence and writing letters, Odile testifying from custody. Wendell pilots on. The beat: legacy — the provision keeps providing.
